title: When the Smile Falls
premise: Ivo Ravensworth hosts the graveyard shift at KRVL, a small-town station where callers keep phoning in—people Ivo buried last week, their voices warm and wrong. The town of Hollow Creek was founded on a covenant: certain families, including Ivo's, were marked to stay unseen so something older could feed undisturbed. When Ivo's childhood imaginary friend, Pell, appears on their porch after twenty years, unchanged and insistent, Ivo learns the founders' ritual was never finished—it was interrupted, and every death since has been the debt accruing interest. To save the town and the one person they love, Ivo must complete the ritual at the standing stones, but finishing it means becoming the thing that keeps the lights on forever. In the end, Ivo chooses to take the founders' place, trading their name and face for Hollow Creek's survival—and Pell, finally, lets them go.
about_author: Wren Eastwick is the pen name of a former late-night radio producer who spent six years answering calls from strangers who sounded like ghosts. They write horror about small towns, dead frequencies, and the people who stay behind to keep the signal alive.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. During the 2 a.m. hour, a caller named Marla asks Ivo to tell her daughter goodbye—Ivo attended Marla's funeral Tuesday. The emotional beat is quiet dread masked by professional calm; Ivo logs the call and pretends it's a prank.

chapters.title: Counting Doors
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Establishing routine: Ivo checks the studio doors twice, keeps every light burning, and avoids mirrors. A brief flashback to childhood rules taught by their grandmother. Beat: controlled fear dressed as habit.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Marla calls again, mid-broadcast, while her widower sits in the lobby. She knows things only Marla knew. Ivo hangs up; the board lights up with nine more lines. Beat: denial cracking.

chapters.title: Pell on the Porch
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Arriving home at dawn, Ivo finds a figure on the porch—Pell, the imaginary friend from age seven, exactly as remembered, down to the mismatched buttons. Pell says, 'You kept the rules. Good.' Beat: uncanny homecoming.

chapters.title: Rules of the House
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Pell explains the household rules were real: don't be seen, don't say your full name aloud, count the doors. Ivo's grandmother didn't invent them; she inherited them. Beat: the past recontextualized as protection.

chapters.title: Hollow Creek Historical Society
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Researching the town founders, Ivo finds a photograph: eleven settlers at the standing stones, and a twelfth figure blurred beyond recognition—the same blur appears in every founding-era photo. Beat: scholarly unease.

chapters.title: The Caller Who Isn't Done
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A new caller, Denny Okafor, died yesterday and doesn't know it yet. He begs Ivo to warn his wife before 'the tall quiet thing' comes for him tonight. Beat: complicity—Ivo fails him.

chapters.title: Nadia
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Introduce Nadia Reyes, the night dispatcher who covers for Ivo's strangeness and brings coffee at 3 a.m. Their unspoken affection surfaces. Beat: warmth against the cold, raising stakes.

chapters.title: What Pell Was For
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Flashback chapter, age seven: Ivo's parents died in the flood year, and Pell appeared the week after, teaching Ivo to be invisible so 'the collectors' would pass over. Beat: grief and gratitude tangled.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In the historical society basement, Ivo finds the Ravensworth family ledger—a ritual text, half-finished, with instructions that stop mid-sentence at page forty. Beat: hope with a hole in it.

chapters.title: Nine Lines Burning
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Every phone line rings at once during broadcast; all nine callers are the recently dead, speaking in unison, reciting Ivo's full name—which they should not know. Beat: exposure; invisibility failing.

chapters.title: The Tall Quiet Thing
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo glimpses it for the first time: a shape at the edge of the parking lot, patient, wearing the posture of someone waiting for a bus that never comes. Beat: first true terror.

chapters.title: Denny's Wife
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo breaks a rule and visits Denny's widow, Ruth, to warn her. Ruth reveals Denny called her too—from the road, an hour after the crash. Beat: guilt deepening; the dead are everywhere.

chapters.title: Pell's Confession
chapters.summary: Pell's POV (first departure). Pell admits it isn't imaginary—it's the unfinished portion of the ritual given a body, bound to the Ravensworth line until the rite completes. It chose to be a friend rather than a warden. Beat: betrayal reframed as devotion.

chapters.title: Station Manager's Meeting
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Management wants Ivo off nights; ratings are up but sponsors are spooked by 'prank calls.' Ivo fights to keep the shift—the dead need somewhere to call. Beat: duty vs. self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Missing Page Forty-One
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The ledger's final page was torn out. The archivist mentions the Ravensworth family donated the collection in 1954—all except one box, sealed, held 'for the last of the line.' Beat: the trap has a shape now.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Box
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In the attic, behind the water heater, Ivo finds the sealed box: page forty-one, a photograph of eleven founders plus a twelfth with Ivo's own face, and a key. Beat: inheritance as sentence.

chapters.title: Page Forty-One
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The missing page describes the completion rite: a name freely surrendered at the stones before the next dark moon, or the town pays in full. Nine days remain. Beat: countdown begins.

chapters.title: Telling Nadia
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo tells Nadia everything over bad diner coffee. Instead of flinching, Nadia says her family came to Hollow Creek the same year—for the same reason. Beat: love against duty, two marked lines finding each other.

chapters.title: The Reyes Covenant
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia reveals her grandmother's role: the Reyes line were the ritual's keepers, meant to finish what the founders started, and they failed in 1954. Her family has been dying early ever since. Beat: shared burden.

chapters.title: Marla's Goodbye
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo finally takes Marla's call on air and says the goodbye her daughter needed. The switchboard goes silent—not empty, satisfied. Beat: purpose found inside horror; the show becomes a ministry.

chapters.title: The Town Notices
chapters.summary: Multiple short POVs. Neighbors begin remembering Ivo—grocers, teachers, the barber. Being seen feels like frostbite. The tall quiet thing moves closer each night. Beat: invisibility collapsing.

chapters.title: Pell's Price
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Pell confesses the cost: whoever completes the rite doesn't die—they persist, nameless, keeping the boundary, as the blurred twelfth founder did. Pell has watched one do it before. Beat: dread of survival's price.

chapters.title: Ruth's Revenge
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Grief-mad Ruth blames Ivo for Denny's death and reports the 'death radio' to the sheriff, forcing Ivo into public view at the worst possible time. Beat: human antagonism sharpening supernatural threat.

chapters.title: Sheriff Dunmore
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The sheriff, surprisingly, believes Ivo—his brother was a caller three years ago. He's been keeping a list: two hundred and six dead since 1954, all on dark moons. Beat: unlikely ally.

chapters.title: The Standing Stones
chapters.summary: Ivo and Nadia's alternating POV. Daylight reconnaissance of the stones; the ground hums, and Ivo's reflection appears in the rock without a mirror. Nadia reads the old Reyes markings aloud. Beat: awe and foreboding.

chapters.title: What the Collectors Take
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Pell explains the economy: the thing feeds on witnessed lives. The founders' bargain bought invisibility for the marked lines—but the rite's interruption left the contract open-ended. Beat: cosmology clarified; stakes total.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Preparation montage: Ivo records farewell messages for everyone they love, trains Nadia on the board, and writes letters that say everything except goodbye. Beat: tender dread; love letters as last wills.

chapters.title: The Broadcast of Names
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On air, Ivo reads all 206 names from the sheriff's list, giving the dead a final witness. The town listens. The tall quiet thing stands outside the studio glass, listening too. Beat: communal catharsis; the enemy drawn near.

chapters.title: It Speaks
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Through the studio glass, the thing speaks with Ivo's mother's voice, offering a deal: walk away, stay invisible, let the town pay. Ivo refuses. Beat: temptation rejected; character crystallized.

chapters.title: Ruth at the Door
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ruth breaks into the station with a shotgun during the dark moon eve. Nadia talks her down, but the noise draws the tall quiet thing to the threshold. Beat: chaos before climax; Nadia endangered.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. The thing takes Nadia instead—not to kill, but to hold as collateral: a keeper needs no hostages unless it fears completion. Ivo has one night. Beat: despair; love weaponized against them.

chapters.title: Pell's Choice
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Pell offers to take Ivo's place—it has a body, a kind of name, enough. But the rite requires a willing soul of the founder's blood. Pell can only carry Ivo to the stones. Beat: sacrifice refused out of love.

chapters.title: The Long Walk
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo walks to the stones through a town gone silent, every porch light burning like an escort, the dead calling in on car radios along the route to keep them company. Beat: elegiac courage.

chapters.title: At the Stones
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Confrontation: the tall quiet thing holds Nadia at the circle's edge. Ivo begins the rite, speaking the surrender, and the thing shows its true face—it is the first Ravensworth, the original coward who fled halfway. Beat: revelation; the monster is kin.

chapters.title: The Surrender
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Climax. Ivo finishes the founders' interrupted words, gives their name to the stones, and steps into the boundary as the twelfth figure. The thing unravels; the dead go quiet, at peace. Beat: triumph purchased with selfhood.

chapters.title: Nameless
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV (unnamed narrator). Aftermath inside the boundary: Ivo persists, faceless in photographs, keeping the lights on in a way no one sees. But the rite had a mercy clause page forty-one never mentioned: one visitor a year may come. Beat: bittersweet survival.

chapters.title: The Visitor
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. One year later, Nadia arrives at the stones on the dark moon with coffee and a portable radio. Ivo can speak for one hour. They spend it saying everything. Beat: love outlasting identity.

chapters.title: KRVL, Still Broadcasting
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia takes the graveyard shift, and the show continues—callers living and otherwise. Pell remains at the station as engineer, finally useful. Beat: continuity; grief transmuted into vocation.

chapters.title: When the Smile Falls
chapters.summary: Unnamed narrator's closing POV. From within the boundary, Ivo watches over Hollow Creek, counting doors that no longer need counting, smiling at last because the watching is done. Final line echoes the title: the smile falls only when it is no longer needed. Beat: peace earned.
